still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US; generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.
The Medicare GLP-1 Bridge pilot has not been revived, Congress has not reopened the ~$41B CBO-scored permanent benefit, and Medicare still pays for no incretin prescribed for weight loss alone.

The September 2027 tri-agency guidance allowing up to 30% premium differentials tied to verified adherence still stands, Illinois's ban on adherence-conditioned premiums is still the only state ban in force, and the suicidal-ideation warning is still off the labels.

population.note: FICTIONAL. Cycling arithmetic: 34.6% ever-used − 24.7% current = 9.9% of adults who used and are off now. About 52% of current users are on a second or later course (12.8 points), and 2.6 points cycled and are off again, so (12.8 + 2.6) / 34.6 ≈ 44.5% of ever-users have cycled. The other ~7.3 points stopped once and have not restarted. This fits one-year persistence near one-third on weekly and oral products (~60% on clinic-administered MariTide and inside conditioned tracks, where losing your premium tier is the cost of stopping) and 36–47% restarting within a year. The 5.8-point rise in ever-use comes mostly from oral amycretin, the alcohol-use-disorder (AUD) label and track enrolment. Age check: 0.20×14.5 + 0.33×25 + 0.24×36 + 0.23×21.5 = 2.9 + 8.25 + 8.64 + 4.95 ≈ 24.7. Income thirds average ~24.7. Users: 24.7% of ~274M adults ≈ 67.7M. FICTIONAL payer mix: commercial ~16.5M (24%, of which ~9.4M are in conditioned metabolic tracks); Medicare ~14.0M (21%); Medicaid ~4.4M (6.5%, ~0.9M of them on the AUD label); legitimate cash ~27.0M (40%, including ~2.4M on calm/focus plans and ~6M who stay on the $149 TrumpRx starting dose indefinitely); imported or counterfeit ~5.8M (8.6%, down from 7.5M after the 2033 tariff shock). Sum: 16.5 + 14.0 + 4.4 + 27.0 + 5.8 = 67.7. On-label AUD users ≈ 2.6M across payers. The bottom third rose only 14 → 17.5: Medicaid AUD coverage and $149 starting doses added users, while about 1.7M gray-market users priced out, about half of them going to TrumpRx starting doses and half stopping. Adult obesity ~32.6%. About 20% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, concentrated in the bottom third, the rural South and adults 65+ without qualifying codes. Pediatric: 1.6% of under-18s are on a drug, ~3.1% of 12–17s and ~0.45% of 6–11s (up from 0.25% after the Feb 2034 semaglutide 6–11 approval). Roughly 60% of new 6–11 starts are Medicaid/CHIP-covered under EPSDT. About 5.3M children live with a parent who has regained after stopping.

access.public_coverage: Medicare (~14.0M users) still pays only through diabetes, CV, CKD, OSA, dementia-risk (obesity plus established CVD) and, since Jan 2033, AUD codes, all behind prior authorisation. FICTIONAL arithmetic: 14.0M × ~$228 average net/month × 12 ≈ $38.3B gross Part D incretin spend before rebate true-up (up from ~$31.6B). Dementia route: ~2.1M × $240 × 12 ≈ $6.0B. AUD route: ~0.8M × $205 × 12 ≈ $2.0B. CMS opened a coding audit of AUD diagnoses in Part D (2034). Medicaid (~4.4M): because AUD is not a weight-loss use, the optional weight-loss exclusion does not apply, so oral semaglutide for AUD is a covered outpatient drug in every state under existing rebate law, behind existing PA criteria. Children 6–11 reach semaglutide through EPSDT medical-necessity rules. 7 states still cover adult weight-loss use, and no state changed its policy. Two state programmes still condition coverage on adherence and BMI progress.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide still sells for $4–30 a month inside India and in 100+ export markets. Chinese tirzepatide-analogue vials sell for $20–60 where patents are not enforced. Delivered to US addresses after the 2033 tariff and export-licence regime, the same product costs ~$90–180. Canadian and Brazilian generics are CAD 45–80 and BRL 160–280. India and China still supply roughly two-thirds of world incretin volume.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Business Group on Health (Nov 2034): 33% of employers cover weight-management use, up from 30%, but ~two-thirds of them now require verified adherence and/or ≥5% weight loss at six months to keep coverage. Unconditional coverage fell to ~11% of employers. Conditioned tracks hold ~9.4M enrollees, inside the ~16.5M commercial users. OPM required FEHB carriers to apply adherence and progress conditions from plan year 2034 (~0.6M FEHB users). Prices: TrumpRx Wegovy pill starting dose $149 and maintenance $199. Foundayo $149–229. Injectable Wegovy/Zepbound $249–299. MariTide $249 direct (~5.8M users). Oral amycretin (approved Feb 2034) has a $1,299 list price and is ~$449 cash direct, with no TrumpRx price yet; ~2.2M users by Dec 2034. Retatrutide ~$399 cash. Orals are ~55% of users, so the pill is now the dominant route. The price shock was in the channel the bottom third used. A Section 232 tariff of 100% on finished peptide drugs and peptide APIs from China and India, plus India's export-licence checks on direct-to-consumer shipments, tripled delivered gray-market prices. Counterfeit serialised pens, which carry higher margins, rose as a share of the shrinking gray market.

GLP-1/amylin unimolecular co-agonist, daily oral (oral amycretin, approved Feb 2034)

GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)

pediatric obesity ages 6–11 (liraglutide incl. generics; weekly semaglutide approved Feb 2034, both with 6-monthly growth-velocity, Tanner staging and eating-disorder screening language)

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. Oral semaglutide for AUD was filed Jan 2032 and approved Jan 2033 (12 months). Oral amycretin and the semaglutide 6–11 sNDA (STEP Young) were both filed in Jan 2033 and both approved in Feb 2034 (13 months). Oral amycretin showed ~21.5% mean weight loss at 72 weeks, matching tirzepatide and injectable amycretin. This realises oral parity for that tier. No oral matches retatrutide's ~24%. Bimagrumab (filed Jul 2032) was approved Aug 2033 only for adults on incretins with high fracture risk; ~150k users at ~$1,100 list. The tirzepatide dementia confirmatory trial met its primary endpoint in Sep 2034 but showed a hip-fracture excess in women 70+, and resubmission is planned for 2035. Implants remain in phase 1–2 and are not on the market. Global incretin market ~$190B (2033). US branded net prices still drift down 3–5% a year. The price rise of this step happened in the import channel, not on branded list prices.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation outside clinic tracks. Oral amycretin's titration nausea is similar to injectable amycretin. Chronic diarrhoea is routinely worked up for EPI.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and bowel obstruction (persistent delayed gastric emptying)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Ileus is labelled, but whether gastroparesis persists after stopping remains disputed in cohort data. The GI arm of the federal MDL and the New Jersey multicounty litigation passed ~38,000 claims by end 2034, naming Novo and Lilly. Plaintiff recruitment now targets cyclers and starting-dose long-term users.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No new labelling. MDL bellwether trials on gastroparesis are set for 2035.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Elevated with rapid weight loss; unchanged.
Still no causal confirmation for acute pancreatitis; absolute risk low. Plaintiffs plead it together with EPI.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; folded into the EPI mass tort.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Medicare hip-fracture HR ~1.3 after more than 2 years and ~1.45 after three or more cycles, worse with EPI malabsorption. The tirzepatide dementia confirmatory trial showed an excess in women 70+.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning retained; DXA code in use; bimagrumab approved (Aug 2033) for high-risk users.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; absolute risk very low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Listed in adverse reactions; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal in adults, including the first year of AUD-label users. The pediatric psychiatric signal concerns restrictive eating.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The FDA postmarketing observational study (Nov 2033) found clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~7% of maintenance-dose users vs ~3.5% of matched controls, dose-related, ~10% on retatrutide. It had too few low-dose users to say anything about calm-plan doses.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: No labelling change. FDA called the findings 'hypothesis-generating'. Two more untitled letters to calm platforms, no enforcement.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months, worse after repeated cycles. About 0.85M gray-market users who were priced out by the 2033 tariffs stopped abruptly and are regaining now.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: None directly; it underpins conditioned coverage.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency, plus thiamine deficiency now reported in AUD-label users who keep drinking. Low ferritin in adolescent girls.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Annual micronutrient panel language on semaglutide and tirzepatide labels; thiamine counselling added to the AUD label.

safety_ledger.effect: Exocrine pancreatic insufficiency after 5+ years of continuous use
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~2× EPI incidence after more than 5 years of continuous semaglutide (~4 vs ~2 per 1,000 person-years). Unsealed MDL documents (Jun 2033) showed Novo safety staff flagged a faecal-elastase decline in a long-term extension cohort in 2027. It reached FDA only as line listings in an aggregate report. The EPI arm of the litigation passed ~54,000 claims, and Novo booked a ~$6.2B reserve. Tirzepatide 5+ year excess is now small but nominally significant (HR ~1.3).
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA demanded the full extension dataset and inspected Novo's pharmacovigilance unit (Form 483, Oct 2033). DOJ issued a civil investigative demand. Novo's chief medical officer resigned. Tirzepatide label got EPI wording (Jun 2034).

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years; effects in children on drug for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of semaglutide follow-up now exist. Cycling effects on bone and pancreas remain poorly characterised. There are no data at all on indefinite starting-dose use.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone-density and growth postmarketing requirements continue, now extended to semaglutide 6–11.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination, substitution)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Adverse-event reports tied to non-approved product passed ~31,000. After the 2033 tariffs, counterfeit pens with cloned codes and domestically re-filled vials made from smuggled API grew as a share of a smaller market. A 2034 CDC cluster linked ~210 Burkholderia infections to re-filled vials in four Southern states, with 3 deaths. Poison-centre calls have plateaued at ~5× 2025 levels.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Section 232 tariff and India export-licence checks (Apr 2033). CBP seizures are flat because volume shifted to domestic re-filling. No statute changed and no state acted.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth deceleration, delayed puberty and restrictive eating in children started young
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The liraglutide 6–11 PMR 36-month update shows height velocity still ~0.6 cm/year below expected in prepubertal starters, with partial catch-up in those who stopped. STEP Young (semaglutide 6–11) showed a similar ~0.5 cm/year deficit over 68 weeks. The Swedish registry ARFID HR is ~1.8. Final adult height is unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Semaglutide 6–11 was approved with the same monitoring language and a medication guide, but no REMS. AAP kept lifestyle-first as the preferred approach for prepubertal children. EMA approved with a narrower BMI threshold.

safety_ledger.effect: Alcohol-related harms on the AUD label (dehydration, alcoholic ketoacidosis, aspiration with vomiting during binge drinking)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: Case series from ED networks describe ketoacidosis and severe dehydration in AUD-label users who binge during titration; ~1 per 2,000 person-years in early data.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label counselling on titration and hydration; postmarketing study required.

food_and_beverage.state: About 41% of US households now have a user. Snack and confectionery volumes are down ~12–14% from 2025 and sugary drinks ~11%. Dollar sales are slightly down for the first time, because premium protein lines no longer offset volume. Zip-code store planning continues. In lower-income zips the 2033 gray-market collapse produced a visible snack rebound, ~3% volume, that Kroger analysts call the 'tariff bounce'.

alcohol.state: US spirits volumes are down ~17% from 2025 and beer ~11%. The AUD label, mandatory Medicaid coverage and EAP pill programmes hit heavy drinkers, who are the industry's volume core. Bourbon producers around Bardstown and Louisville cut ~1,800 jobs and slowed barrel laydown. Distributors consolidate. Non-alcoholic and 'calm' drinks grow but stay under 5% of category dollars.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat. Bar and late-night revenue is down sharply in mid-sized Midwestern cities. Casual dining runs portion tiers and drops dessert pages. QSR value menus gain in Memphis-type markets as priced-out users regain.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep shrinking. Resale and stretch serve cyclers, and the regain wave in lower-income zips is lifting size-up returns at mass retailers. Structured athletic wear and tailoring keep growing.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. Track contracts require InBody scans, which feeds budget chains. Bimagrumab prescriptions bundle with clinic coaching. Pediatric 'family strength' programmes grew after the 6–11 approval as upper-income parents chose them over the drug.

insurance.state: Employer coverage rose to 33% but became conditional, with ~two-thirds requiring adherence or progress. Pharmacy trend ~+7%, driven by oral amycretin prior-authorisation requests and AUD claims. Adherence premium differentials are now standard at large self-insured firms. Part D premiums rose again for 2034 and 2035, and CMS is auditing AUD coding. Medicaid budgets absorb ~0.9M AUD users without any state having chosen to.

pharma.state: The market is still growing, but Novo took the hits: a ~$6.2B litigation reserve, a DOJ inquiry and leadership turnover, at the same moment its oral amycretin launched strongly. Lilly faces GI claims and new EPI wording. Amgen grew on tracks. Litigation-finance firms fund plaintiff recruitment. Indian exporters lost US direct-to-consumer volume and redirected it to Gulf, Latin American and African markets.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: The body still reads as how you are paid, and now also as when the tariff hit you. Lifted and scanned means covered and coached. Thin and soft with a monthly clinic bruise means a track. Slow-thin on a pill you never titrated past the starting dose means cash at $149. Regaining in 2034 in Memphis or Jackson means your vial supplier disappeared. A child's six-monthly growth chart is a status document in Bethesda and a clinic form in South Memphis.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: Muscle remains the class uniform, and 'off-drug lean' remains the elite boast in Charlotte and Austin. Upper-income parents largely refused semaglutide for prepubertal children after its approval and buy family strength programmes. Medicaid children, newly covered under EPSDT, make up most new 6–11 starts. In the Mississippi Delta the 2033 price shock produced the first visible mass regain, and it is read locally as a federal decision.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Shared meals are shorter and drier. Bars in Dayton and Toledo now host 'pill nights' with non-alcoholic menus. Bread Alone claims ~1,000 congregations and holds communal 'full table' suppers framed against the pediatric approval. School-lunch fights are now about whether nurses should record medication for 6–11s.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Apps added an 'on AUD treatment' tag beside 'calm plan', and users treat it as a disclosure about drinking more than about weight. Couples where one partner stopped drinking on the pill report the familiar mismatch plus a social one: the old bar friends drift.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: In the upper tier, appetite, thirst and craving are all noise a subscription manages. In lower-income communities appetite became political in 2033: the tariff that took the vials away is called 'the hunger tax'. The backlash is now visible and loosely joined. In May 2034 the 'Let Them Grow' rally drew ~60,000 MAHA parents, Unmuted chapters and Bread Alone congregations to the Mall after the pediatric approval and the Novo documents. Fat-acceptance revivalists held a separate march in Oakland, and each side's speakers called the other's movement 'compromised by pharma'.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: The FDA observational study puts clinically meaningful anhedonia at ~7% of maintenance-dose users vs ~3.5% of controls, ~10% on retatrutide. About 2.4M people are on calm/focus plans, up from 1.3M: low-dose Wegovy pill or Foundayo at $149–199 plus a $39–59 fee. Platforms now screen every applicant with AUDIT-C, and ~35% of subscribers are written on the AUD label. That lets the platforms advertise 'craving-free' on-label to drinkers. The anhedonia rate at low doses is still unmeasured.
interior_life.framing: The platforms sell a feature ('quiet the noise', and now 'quiet the bottle'). Manufacturers say 'food noise' and, for AUD, 'reduced heavy drinking days'. HR calls it steadiness. Clinicians call it dose-related blunting. After the Novo documents, Unmuted calls it 'a sedative with a cover-up attached'.
interior_life.effect_on_work: About 9.4M employees are in conditioned tracks, and missing a clinic shot or a pill-log sync can move a family's premium tier. EAPs at trucking, warehousing and call-centre employers now offer the AUD pill directly. FMCSA guidance (2033) says on-label AUD treatment does not disqualify a commercial driver if it is disclosed to the medical examiner, but it is silent on calm plans. Benefit brokers buy de-identified 'focus' cohorts from the platforms. The two EEOC charges remain unresolved.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off' memoir is now its own shelf, and 'dry' stand-up about life after the pill is a Netflix genre. Live-music venues in Columbus and Louisville cut nights because bar margins vanished. Sportsbook handle per account keeps falling in insured suburbs. Ambient streaming tiers are marketed to calm subscribers.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: The shot date and the pill window, nothing by mouth for 30 minutes, structure couples' mornings. Couples therapists report a new presentation: one partner who quit drinking on the pill and finds the other's drinking intolerable, while the drinking partner finds the sober one absent.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The backlash got its rally and its documents but no legislation. No state acted, and Congress held two hearings, on the Novo disclosures and the pediatric approval, without a bill. The tariff, sold as safety and sovereignty, is the first incretin policy with a visible losing constituency: Delta and Memphis gray-market users. 'Sedated electorate' claims still lack turnout evidence.

state.regulatory_posture: Federal, routine and permissive on approvals, punitive on imports. FDA approved the AUD label, oral amycretin, semaglutide 6–11 and bimagrumab, inspected Novo's safety unit and sent more untitled letters to calm platforms. No state legislature or agency acted. Illinois's ban is still the only one.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No new subsidy. OPM required adherence and progress conditions for FEHB anti-obesity coverage from plan year 2034. Medicaid AUD coverage became effectively mandatory under existing rebate law, with no new statute. The 2027 tri-agency 30% guidance stands.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Deeper in practice. Clinic records, PBM fills, smart-pill-bottle logs (now bundled with oral amycretin starter kits) and telehealth mood check-ins flow to wellness vendors under consent. FEHB carriers receive adherence feeds. CMS's AUD coding audit pulls telehealth AUDIT-C records. Two state Medicaid programmes still condition coverage.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE covers the AUD label under existing rules, and the Army recruit oral pilot continues without expansion. FMCSA's 2033 guidance covers on-label AUD use by drivers but not calm plans.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: In Apr 2033 a Section 232 tariff of 100% on finished peptide drugs and peptide APIs from China and India took effect, paired with an interim US–India trade deal in which India agreed to export-licence checks on direct-to-consumer incretin shipments. Beijing filed a WTO complaint. Indian exporters redirected volume. Smuggled API now feeds domestic re-filling operations. Novo's Danish and US plants and Lilly's US plants are exempt.

events.event: FDA approves the Wegovy pill for moderate-to-severe alcohol use disorder, the first incretin addiction indication; the same week Novo files oral amycretin (21.5% weight loss at 72 weeks) and a semaglutide sNDA for children 6–11
events.driver: new_indications: alcohol_use_disorder; next_gen_launch: oral_parity (filing); new_indications: pediatric_under_12 (filing)

events.event: A 100% Section 232 tariff on Chinese and Indian peptide drugs and APIs takes effect alongside Indian export-licence checks; delivered prices for mail-order semaglutide vials roughly triple to $90–180 and an estimated 1.7 million US gray-market users drop out or switch

Documents unsealed in the federal incretin MDL show Novo safety staff flagged a pancreatic-enzyme decline in a 2027 extension cohort that reached FDA only as line listings; Novo books a $6.2B reserve, its CMO resigns, and GI and EPI claims pass 90,000 by late 2034

OPM tells FEHB carriers that from 2034 anti-obesity drug coverage requires verified adherence and 5% weight loss at six months; by the 2034 benefits season two-thirds of covering employers impose similar conditions and track enrolment reaches 9.4 million

FDA approves oral amycretin, the first pill to match tirzepatide's weight loss, and weekly semaglutide for children 6–11 with growth-monitoring language; most new pediatric starts come through Medicaid under EPSDT

'Let Them Grow' rally draws about 60,000 MAHA parents, Unmuted chapters and Bread Alone congregations to the National Mall against the pediatric approval and the Novo documents; fat-acceptance groups march separately in Oakland

open_tensions: Semaglutide is now approved for 6–11-year-olds who grow about half a centimetre a year more slowly on it. The children starting it are mostly on Medicaid, while the parents best able to watch growth charts are opting out. Nobody will know adult height for a decade.
The AUD label turned calm plans partly on-label. 2.4 million people now buy blunting with an AUDIT-C score attached, CMS is auditing the coding, and the low-dose anhedonia rate is still unmeasured.

The 2033 tariff shrank the gray market but pushed users either to $149 starting doses with no efficacy data for indefinite use, or to regain. Domestic re-filling from smuggled API is now killing people in the South.

Novo's documents gave 90,000 plaintiffs a story and gave the backlash a villain. Novo's oral amycretin is still the fastest-growing launch in the class, and conditioned coverage makes stopping costly for the people most worried about their pancreas.

prose.headline: The Pill Caught Up. The Vials Got Expensive. And Now Your Nine-Year-Old Qualifies.
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2034 roughly one American adult in four takes an incretin drug, about sixty-eight million people, and more than a third have tried one. The rise was faster than in any earlier two years, and it rests on three things that happened in Washington and one in a laboratory.

The laboratory result was a pill. In February 2034 the FDA approved oral amycretin, Novo's daily tablet, which in its phase 3 trial took off about a fifth of body weight, as much as the injectables that had defined the decade. People who would never inject now swallow, and the pill is now the dominant route. It costs about $449 a month in cash and sits behind prior authorisation everywhere else. The Wegovy starting pill is still $149 through TrumpRx. Six million people now stay on that starting dose indefinitely because it is what they can afford, a regimen nobody has studied.

The first Washington change was a label. In January 2033 the Wegovy pill was approved for alcohol use disorder. Because that is not a weight-loss use, Medicaid has to cover it, and so does Medicare, which still pays nothing for weight alone. Bourbon country noticed first. Around Bardstown the distilleries cut shifts, and in Dayton the bars hold pill nights. The telehealth calm platforms noticed too. They now screen every new subscriber for drinking, and about a third of their 2.4 million customers are written on the alcohol label, which lets the companies advertise freedom from craving to drinkers. CMS has begun auditing the diagnoses.

The second was a tariff. In April 2033 a 100 percent duty on Chinese and Indian peptide drugs came into force, along with an Indian promise to check exports to American mailboxes. The Indian vial that cost forty dollars now costs a hundred and forty. About 1.7 million people left the gray market. Half went to the $149 pill and half stopped, and in Memphis and the Delta the regain is visible on the street. People there call it the hunger tax. The trade did not end. Smuggled powder is now refilled into vials in back rooms in Mississippi and Alabama, and this year a cluster of infections from those vials killed three people.

The third was a condition. The federal employee health programme now pays for weight drugs only for members who prove they take them and lose five percent in six months. Most employers that still cover the drugs do the same. Coverage technically rose, to a third of employers, but it now comes with a log, a scan and a premium tier that drops if the log goes quiet. Nine and a half million workers live inside those tracks.

The scandal landed in the middle of all this. In June 2033 documents unsealed in the federal litigation showed Novo's own safety staff had flagged a pancreatic warning sign in 2027, and it reached regulators only as rows in a table. Novo set aside six billion dollars, its medical chief resigned, and the lawsuits over stomach paralysis and pancreatic failure passed ninety thousand. Novo's new pill is still the fastest launch in the class.

Then the children. In February 2034 weekly semaglutide was approved for six-to-eleven-year-olds, with the same instruction as before: measure height every six months and screen for disordered eating. The trial showed the same slower growth. Parents in Bethesda and Plano mostly declined and bought family strength classes. Most new starts are Medicaid children, covered under federal rules for children's medical necessity. In May sixty thousand people rallied on the Mall under the banner Let Them Grow. No state passed anything. From a distance the country looks steadier, drinks less and eats less. Up close it is being logged.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Lorna Pruitt sets her alarm for 5:10 so she can take the pill thirty minutes before coffee, with four ounces of water and nothing else. It is the $149 starting dose. It has been the $149 starting dose for fourteen months, since the Mumbai seller's vials went to a hundred and forty-five and then stopped coming. Her jeans have stopped getting looser. They have not started getting tighter, and that is what she is paying for.

At the bus depot on Lamar she runs dispatch. A driver named Curtis leans in the window and asks if the drinking pill shows up on a drug test. She tells him to ask the examiner, because that is what the memo says. He says his cousin got it free through TennCare. She says good for his cousin.

At lunch she eats half a turkey sandwich and wraps the rest for later. Later she won't eat it.

At four she picks up Kiara, who is ten, from the clinic on Elvis Presley Boulevard. The nurse measured her again, four feet six and a quarter. They wrote it on the chart, and Kiara asked to see the line. It bends a little. Kiara gets the shot on Sundays. TennCare pays. The nurse said the line is still inside the band.

At home her husband has the news on: people on the Mall holding signs with children's height charts. Kiara watches for a minute and asks if those are kids like her.

Lorna says no, those are other kids, and turns it to the cooking channel, and Kiara watches a woman make bread.

least_plausible_claims.quote: ~6M who stay on the $149 TrumpRx starting dose indefinitely
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism and magnitude: about 6M people (22% of the 27M legitimate-cash users) are said to sit on a starting dose indefinitely. No chain explains why that many stay at a sub-therapeutic dose rather than titrating, and the 'no data at all' on it makes the headcount an assertion.

least_plausible_claims.quote: The bottom third rose only 14 → 17.5: Medicaid AUD coverage and $149 starting doses added users, while about 1.7M gray-market users priced out
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude: a 3.5-point rise is roughly +3.2M net users in the bottom third while about 1.7M gray-market users, concentrated there, leave. That needs about 4M gross gains. The named sources (≤0.9M Medicaid AUD plus about 0.85M redirected to $149 doses) do not cover it.
Magnitude: the note gives 3.1% of 12–17s and 0.45% of 6–11s. Equal-width age bands weight these to about 1.2% of under-18s, not 1.6%, and the starting-world pediatric figures have the same gap.

rationale.badness: Premiums, FEHB and 9.4M enrollees are conditioned on pill logs and scans, so autonomy is badly hit (state/conditioning_or_surveillance, effect_on_work). Children on Medicaid are started on a drug with a known growth deficit while the best-resourced parents opt out (open_tensions, thinness_and_class). The tariff produced the 'hunger tax' regain wave and domestic re-filled vials causing Burkholderia deaths. About 90k litigation claims, regain after abrupt stopping and the unmeasured low-dose anhedonia add to this. The result is structural and partly invisible, but it stays a harder 2032 rather than a collapse, so I stop at 7.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Most drivers are visible in events (AUD label, pediatric approval, oral amycretin, Novo scandal and litigation, OPM conditioning, Mall rally). A Section 232 action plus an India deal inside about 15 months also sits awkwardly with `state_action: none`. The 1.7M exit figure is a bare estimate.

least_plausible_claims.quote: Oral amycretin (approved Feb 2034) has a $1,299 list price and is ~$449 cash direct, with no TrumpRx price yet; ~2.2M users by Dec 2034.
least_plausible_claims.why: Magnitude and mechanism: 2.2M users within about ten months of launch, at $449 cash with prior authorisation everywhere else, has no payer breakdown behind it. The 2032 pipeline note never mentions oral amycretin or a phase 3 filing, so the Jan 2033 filing appears from nowhere.

rationale.badness: Usage reaches 24.7% of adults and premium tiers hinge on pill logs for ~9.4M workers (`effect_on_work`). Medicaid children make up most new 6–11 starts on a drug with a known ~0.5 cm/year growth deficit, while upper-income parents opt out (`thinness_and_class`). The tariff pushes the poorest into regain or back-room vials that killed three people, and ~90k litigants plus the Novo documents add distrust. This is a harder society with clear new losers and quiet normalisation, but no collapse, so it sits at 6.5, not higher.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: Most drivers are visibly realised in fields and events: AUD and 6–11 approvals, oral amycretin parity, the Novo scandal, EPI/GI litigation, the rally and OPM conditioning. `price_path: shock_up` is met only in the import channel, since branded prices still drift down, and the tariff and OPM mandate are heavy federal actions despite `state_action: none` (claim 2). mechanism: Most changes have chains: the AUD label forces Medicaid coverage, the tariff pushes users to $149 starting doses or regain, and AUDIT-C routes calm plans onto the AUD label. The 6M indefinite starting-dose users and the fast oral amycretin uptake are asserted rather than shown (claims 1 and 3). magnitude: Adult use of 24.7% and ever-use of 34.6% are inside the envelope, and the approval timings (12–13 months from filing) obey the rules. The age bands, income thirds, payer mix (sums to 67.7M), cycling arithmetic and Medicare spend ($38.3B, $6.0B and $2.0B) all reconcile. Minor gaps are the tripling arithmetic and a pediatric 1.6% headline that exceeds what the age-band figures imply, as in 2032.
rationale.generativity: The prose scene is a Memphis dispatcher on the $149 pill, a driver asking about drug tests, a ten-year-old with a bending growth chart and a rally on TV. It shows rather than explains, and each beat ties to a world field. The JSON adds texture too: pill nights in Dayton, the 'hunger tax', 'dry' stand-up and smart-pill-bottle bundles.

least_plausible_claims.quote: because AUD is not a weight-loss use, the optional weight-loss exclusion does not apply, so oral semaglutide for AUD is a covered outpatient drug in every state under existing rebate law, behind existing PA criteria
least_plausible_claims.why: Mechanism: it asserts that Medicaid AUD coverage became effectively mandatory in all states with no statute, rule or litigation. States can still restrict through formulary and PA, and the candidate shows no chain for ~0.9M Medicaid AUD users.

Magnitude and mechanism: a $449 cash, prior-authorisation-gated oral reaches 2.2M users in under ten months. The candidate shows no payer or channel path for that uptake, and the figure is hard to square with the payer mix.

Mechanism and driver fidelity: a 100% tariff plus licence checks would roughly double a price, yet the world has it tripling ($40 to $90–180). The tariff and India trade deal are sweeping federal executive actions that sit uneasily with `state_action: none`, and branded prices do not move at all, which makes `shock_up` thin.

rationale.badness: Premium tiers tied to adherence logs for ~9.4M workers, plus smart-pill-bottle feeds and CMS audits of AUDIT-C records, push autonomy and surveillance harms high. Inequality is also high: the bottom third is priced out of the gray market into mass regain, Medicaid children make up most new 6–11 starts while Bethesda parents opt out, and Burkholderia vials killed people in the South. Harm is partly visible and discussed (rally, MDL, FDA study), which holds epistemic and cohesion scores in the mid-range. It is a recognisably harder society with new losers, not a collapse.
rationale.plausibility: driver_fidelity: All drivers are traceable to events and fields, with the AUD, pediatric 6–11 and oral amycretin approvals falling inside the allowed timing windows. `shock_up` is realised only in the import channel while branded prices are unchanged, and a tariff/trade deal and OPM mandate sit awkwardly with `state_action: none`. mechanism: The Medicaid-AUD 'mandatory under existing rebate law' chain is asserted, the tripling of prices from a 100% tariff is stretched, and rapid oral amycretin uptake has no shown path. The 2033-06 event also cites claims 'by late 2034', and the prose says Lorna's $149 dose has run 14 months when the tariff was about 20 months earlier. magnitude: Adult use (24.7), ever-use (34.6), income thirds, age bands, payer sum (67.7M) and Medicare spend arithmetic all reconcile inside the envelope. The pediatric figures (1.6% under 18 vs 3.1% of 12–17 and 0.45% of 6–11) do not quite multiply out, and the 2.2M amycretin figure is aggressive.
rationale.generativity: The prose has a concrete protagonist with a 5:10 pill routine and a Memphis bus depot, a dispatcher exchange about drug tests and TennCare, and a child's growth-chart line, all grounded in specific places. The world fields add many implied scenes: pill nights in Dayton, the Mall rally, bourbon layoffs and the 'hunger tax'.
